week.title: FX Daily: Dollar holds gains into midterms
week.desc: At the start of a very busy week for FX markets, the dollar is largely holding onto recent gains. In focus are the US midterms, where betting markets attach a 70% probability to a clean sweep for the Democrats. Away from politics, we'll receive updates on the US jobs market this week and are expecting rate hikes in the UK, Australia and Sweden

week.title: The election will be good news, regardless of outcome, says Morgan Stanley’s chief stock-market strategist
week.desc: Morgan Stanley’s chief stock-market strategist, Mike Wilson, said the midterm elections are a classic “clearing event” whose outcome at this point doesn’t really matter.

week.title: Tech stocks have made big V-shaped rebounds five times in 30 months — and now Deutsche Bank forecasts another bounce
week.desc: Positioning among equity investors in tech stocks is consistent with much slower earnings growth than the sector is achieving. Deutsche Bank thinks it’s time to go overweight once again as the risk-reward profile favors a sector that is suddenly out of fashion.

week.title: UBS’s Fowler Says Market Is Underpricing the Length of AI Cycle
week.desc: Hyperscaler valuations look attractive after the recent AI unwind as the market prices in a shorter AI cycle than is likely to play out, according to Gerry Fowler, chief European equity strategist and head of derivatives at UBS AG.

week.title: Stock Bulls Are Betting on a Bounce After the Midterms
week.desc: Any post-vote selloff is likely to be short-lived, Morgan Stanley’s Wilson says.

week.title: Citi throws in the towel on hyperscalers after a key stock-market bet misfires
week.desc: Hyperscalers and growth plays have underperformed amid a sharp rotation.

week.title: Greek Stocks to Suffer Outflows on MSCI Upgrade, JPMorgan Says
week.desc: Greek stocks will suffer outflows as MSCI Inc.’s upgrade of the country to developed-market status forces emerging-market trackers to sell, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co. strategists.

week.title: Citi FX Traders Like Carry But Say It’s No ‘Set-and-Forget’ Bet
week.desc: Citigroup Inc.’s US currency desk expects the carry trade to keep offering opportunities for investors even though the strategy may struggle to replicate a period of standout returns.

week.title: Tech Sell-Off Marks 'Crisis of Confidence,' Says Jordan Jackson
week.desc: Disappointing US megacap earnings accelerated a rotation out of AI-related tech last week, triggering a sharp selloff as investors shifted toward smaller-cap and more defensive areas. Jordan Jackson, Global Market Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, discusses the overblown AI selloff and how he expects to see markets move after midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

week.title: FX Daily: Democratic sweep can weigh on the dollar
week.desc: We don’t expect today’s US midterm results to cause structural shifts in FX, but the dollar may face some short-term pressure should the Democrats secure both the House (widely expected) and the Senate (close call). Elsewhere, a dovish hike by the RBA has hit AUD, but we remain optimistic on the outlook for the currency beyond the near term

week.title: JPM’s Michele Tells US Treasury ‘Get Rid of the 20-Year’
week.desc: Bob Michele, global head of fixed income at JPMorgan Asset Management, offers guidance to the US Treasury ahead of the November 2026 quarterly refunding announcement. He says the equity market “is going to go through some of its demons” to the benefit of the bond market and provides his outlook for bond yields. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

week.title: Palantir stock is down 8%. Analysts say bookings growth is to blame.
week.desc: Analysts at Morgan Stanley pointed to a slowdown in a number of bookings metrics in the third quarter as worth picking at.

week.title: UBS Traders See ‘Combustible Setup’ for S&P 500 Rally After Vote
week.desc: US stocks may be poised for a year-end rebound as favorable seasonality and low hedge fund positioning set the stage for a potential rally after Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to UBS Securities.

week.title: An overlooked energy source could solve AI’s power crunch — and these 2 stocks are prime plays
week.desc: Geothermal technology is in the early stages of its own shale revolution, Morgan Stanley says.

week.title: S&P 500 is looking over the edge of a technical cliff — what happens if it falls off?
week.desc: Falling below 7,500 would lead to a dramatic increase in selling pressure and volatility, a J.P. Morgan strategist says, and that could end in a full-blown correction

week.title: FX Daily: Blue wave price action a preview of what’s to come
week.desc: For a change, opinion polls proved correct, and the Democrats delivered a stunning victory in the US midterm elections. Short-dated US rates and the dollar are a little weaker, while equity futures are busy reclaiming some of their 2-3% losses seen overnight on fears that the AI data centre build-out would slow. Price action previews what could come in 2027

week.title: Rates Spark: A blue wave in the US and euro inflation
week.desc: A decisive election result supports immediate sentiment, but the prospect of tighter AI regulation could add to jitters about the tech sector. A president now potentially focusing more on foreign policy leaves oil and tariff risks in focus as sources of rate volatility. Eurozone headline inflation is expected to rise to 4%

week.title: A delayed landing for GBP rates
week.desc: EUROPE: GBP rates seem to have drifted too high versus Bank of England expectations, which we attribute to a significant risk premium stemming from prior trading trauma. We therefore see rates lower across the curve, but only once inflation risks settle and US rates ease lower. Meanwhile, structural supply factors will keep the sterling curve steeper

week.title: Euro rates have good reason to be nervous
week.desc: EUROPE: Easing inflation fears should bring euro rates down by mid-2027, but the path lower will be bumpy. We shift our attention from oil to inflation data and expect markets to react anxiously to upside surprises. Rising bond issuance outside the US government and AI could catch markets by surprise, but that is not our base case

week.title: The AI trade has been ‘sold to death’ but Goldman strategist highlights silver lining from Democratic sweep
week.desc: Corporate decision makers may decide to accelerate their plans to expand compute capacity and take advantage of the status quo rather than risk a new administration and different rules in 2029

week.title: Uzbekistan rates stay on hold, but hopes for 2027 cuts remain
week.desc: COMMONWEALTH OF INDEPENDENT STATES: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan kept its policy rate unchanged at 14.00%, as expected, but delivered a more hawkish message than in September. Higher inflation and GDP forecasts suggest that easing in 2026 is now less likely. But we still see scope for cuts in 2027, assuming continued fiscal restraint and potential FX strength

week.title: FX Daily: A dollar downturn lacks the rate ingredient
week.desc: The post-midterm dollar correction requires a worsening of USD rate differentials to turn into a downturn. But as oil prices fall, other central banks are facing similar or even larger dovish repricing than the Fed. Data is key now, but indications are that they won’t turn USD-negative soon. Today, expect a hike in the UK and rate holds in Norway and Mexico

week.title: UBS Cuts London Jobs, European Stocks Hit Fresh Record
week.desc: UBS has slashed about two hundred positions in London in recent weeks as the integration of Credit Suisse nears its end. The cuts were announced internally in recent weeks, according to people familiar with the matter. The reductions were carried out across the bank’s units, including wealth management and investment banking, they said. European stocks surpassed their prior closing record high as the region extended an outperformance driven by a rotation out of the artificial intelligence trade and a strong earnings season. The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day

week.title: Rates Spark: Treasury heat from tech flight - but for how long?
week.desc: A creeping move lower in equities would eventually be ignored by Treasuries. But a large dump in equities would not. Treasuries are so far very much in vogue. In Europe, bond spreads are widening again as we head into another weekend of street unrest. Friday sees US jobs data competing for the spotlight, although Thursday's low claims were broadly ignored

week.title: FX Daily: Tech collapses, FX shrugs

FX participants so far see this as an idiosyncratic re-pricing of the tech sector, rather than a harbinger of recession. Expect defensive FX to outperform, rather than a broad dollar decline
